small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_SP to 128 or 256 and BLOCK_OC to 32 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3; the current 64×64 with num_warps=4 underutilizes the 4090's SMs given the small grid (16 × 1 × ~256). Wrap in `triton.autotune` over {(BLOCK_SP=128,BLOCK_OC=32,nw=4),(128,64,8),(256,32,8),(64,128,8)}.
- Hoist the `ic` loop outside the (kd,kh,kw) loops and load weights into registers once per (kd,kh,kw,oc) tile; better, swap loop order so the input read for a given (id_q,ih_q,iw_q) is reused across all OC. Also precompute `IH*IW`, `ID*IH*IW`, `OC*KD*KH*KW` as scalars outside the loops.
- Use `tl.dot` by reshaping the inner ic-loop into a GEMM: tile K=IC, accumulate `x[BLOCK_SP, BLOCK_K] @ w[BLOCK_K, BLOCK_OC]` per kernel position — this exploits tensor cores instead of the current outer-product fmas.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a true im2col-style GEMM: per output tile (N, OC_tile, SP_tile), gather contributing input rows into a [BLOCK_SP, IC*KD*KH*KW] patch (with stride/pad index math) and multiply by a [IC*KD*KH*KW, BLOCK_OC] weight matrix using `tl.dot`. This collapses the 27× kernel-position loop into a single GEMM-K reduction with tensor cores.
- Alternative: scatter-add design — one program per (N, IC_tile, input-spatial tile) computes `input × weight` outer products and `tl.atomic_add`s into the output grid at strided/padded positions. This avoids the inverse-stride divisibility test and the wasted lanes when SD>1 (currently 7/8 of (kd,kh,kw,sp) combos are masked out).
- Fold the bias add and the closed-form epilogue `y = (2x+b_extra)*x + x = 2x² + x*b_extra + x` into the GEMM epilogue (already done) and use channels-last (NDHWC) output layout so the OC tile stores are contiguous, improving store bandwidth.
